instructions: Finely chop the onion. Mince all 8 garlic cloves and keep them in two piles of 4.
Heat 1 tbsp of the olive oil in a large, deep sauté pan with a lid over medium heat. Add the onion and cook it for about 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until it's soft and see-through.
Add the first 4 garlic cloves and stir for about 30 seconds, until you can smell them.
Add the 1 1/2 cups rice and stir for 1 minute, until every grain is coated in the oil.
Add the crushed tomatoes, 2 1/2 cups of the stock, the 1 1/2 cups peas, 1 tsp of the salt and a pinch of pepper. Stir and bring it to a boil over medium high heat.
Turn the heat to low, cover the pan and cook for 15 minutes, until the rice is just tender and has soaked up the liquid. No peeking.
Meanwhile, if the shrimp aren't peeled and deveined, do that now. Pat them dry with paper towels and sprinkle them with the last 1/2 tsp salt and a pinch of pepper.
Heat the remaining 2 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over high heat until it shimmers. Lay the shrimp in a single layer and leave them for 1 minute, until they're golden underneath.
Flip them and cook the other side for 1 minute. They don't need to be cooked through yet. Transfer them to a plate.
Turn the heat to medium low. Add the 2 tbsp butter and the other 4 garlic cloves and stir for about 30 seconds, until the garlic smells sweet. Don't let it brown.

Squeeze half the lemon. That should be about 1 tbsp of juice. Add it to the skillet with the remaining 1/2 cup stock and scrape up the browned bits. Let it bubble for 3 to 5 minutes, until it's reduced by about a third, then take it off the heat.

When the rice is done, take the pan off the heat. Lay the shrimp on top of the rice, put the lid back on and leave it for 5 minutes, until the shrimp are pink and opaque all the way through. Cut one in half to check.
Meanwhile, chop 2 tbsp of the parsley and cut the other lemon half into wedges.
Spoon the garlic butter sauce over the shrimp and rice and scatter the parsley on top.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of the lemon.
method_notes: Simply Delicious (the lead) cooks the rice in the pan with onion, garlic, crushed tomatoes, stock and peas, sears the shrimp hard in a separate pan, makes a garlic butter sauce with wine, stock and lemon there, and lets the shrimp finish by steaming on the rice. Cook.me (the Diethood recipe, whose own page blocked reading; it shows 13 reviews, a reviewCount, not a ratingCount) is quicker, stirring instant rice into garlic butter with the shrimp, Parmesan and a splash of milk. This follows the lead with stock in place of the wine and 1 1/2 cups rice instead of 2 1/2 so it suits four plates. Done honestly it takes about 40 minutes, not 20.
